text: More than 300 years ago, Europe was coming out of more than a hundred years of wars over religion.
In England, John Locke wrote that a government should rest on the agreement of the people it rules.
src: 1685 to 1815 (approximate) / In the later 17th century Europe was emerging from more than a century of religious war
John Locke / Two Treatises of Government, which grounded government in the consent of the governed

text: Its thinkers believed that reason and evidence, not old customs alone, should guide what people know and believe.
The thinker Immanuel Kant gave the movement a motto: “dare to know”.
src: reason, evidence and free enquiry, not tradition or authority alone, should guide knowledge, belief and government
In 1784 Immanuel Kant defined enlightenment / gave it a motto from the Roman poet Horace, “Sapere aude”, dare to know

text: In Paris, Denis Diderot edited the Encyclopédie, twenty-eight big books with more than 70,000 articles.
When the government took away its permission to print, he carried on in secret.
src: the first volume of the Encyclopédie appeared, edited by Denis Diderot / in Paris / twenty-eight volumes with more than 70,000 articles
in 1759 the government revoked its licence to publish, but Diderot, left as sole editor when d’Alembert withdrew, carried on in secret

text: The writer Voltaire spoke up for people treated unjustly and called for tolerance between faiths.
With Émilie du Châtelet, he spread Isaac Newton’s science in France.
src: Voltaire, born François-Marie Arouet, wrote plays, histories, satires and pamphlets, campaigned for the victims of injustice / Voltaire’s Treatise on Tolerance
he and his companion Émilie du Châtelet worked to spread Newton’s physics in France

text: Their ideas helped inspire the American and French revolutions and their declarations of people’s rights.
But for a long time these rights were kept from most women and from enslaved people.
src: inspired the American and French revolutions / the declarations of rights of 1776 and 1789
though the rights it proclaimed long excluded most women and the enslaved

text: Enlightenment ideas, like human rights and a free press, still shape how people talk about government.
A list of rights for everyone, written more than 70 years ago, follows in their footsteps.
src: The Enlightenment shaped much of the modern world’s vocabulary of politics: natural and human rights, the separation of powers, government by consent, freedom of conscience and of the press
The Universal Declaration of Human Rights of 1948 stands in the line of the declarations of 1776 and 1789
